c.tagline: An adobe desert oasis town ringed by geysers, salt flats, and the otherworldly Valle de la Luna
langs: Kunza (nearly extinct Atacameño language, largely ceremonial)

card: Widely accepted at hotels and tour agencies; cash useful for small shops

taxi.fareNote: Most sightseeing (Valle de la Luna, El Tatio geysers, salt flats) is done via organized tour rather than taxi

emergency.note: 133 for police, 131 for medical emergencies; response times can be slower given the town's remoteness

religion: Indigenous Atacameño spiritual traditions (practiced alongside Christianity by some)
walk: San Pedro's small adobe town center is walkable; nearly all major attractions (Valle de la Luna, geysers, salt flats) require an organized tour or rental vehicle

safety.safety: Very safe town, though the surrounding desert and high-altitude sites demand preparation for sun, cold nights, and altitude
safety.crime: Very low crime; the main risks are altitude sickness and extreme desert temperature swings

hood_landmark.San Pedro Town Center: San Pedro's adobe church and central plaza
hood_landmark.Valle de la Luna (day-trip): The moon-like eroded salt formations of Valle de la Luna
hood_landmark.El Tatio Geysers (day-trip): El Tatio's steaming high-altitude geyser field
hood_landmark.Salar de Atacama (day-trip): The Salar de Atacama's flamingo-filled salt lagoons
hood_landmark.Laguna Cejar / Altiplanic Lagoons (day-t: Laguna Cejar's dense, buoyant swimming waters

avoid.reason: Unlit dirt streets at night and occasional theft from hostels and parked bikes — keep valuables secured.

hood_desc: The compact adobe town with most hotels, restaurants, and tour agencies; the practical base for the entire Atacama region.
A surreal lunar-like desert landscape a short drive from town, best visited at sunset when the colors intensify.
One of the world's highest-altitude geyser fields, best visited near sunrise when the steam plumes are most dramatic against the cold air.
A vast salt flat south of town, home to flamingo colonies and some of the clearest reflections in the Atacama.
A cluster of salt lagoons near San Pedro so dense with minerals that swimmers float effortlessly, popular for a late-afternoon dip.

water.note: Local tap water is high in minerals including arsenic; drink bottled or filtered.

transit.sys: Tour agency shuttles and local taxis; no formal public bus network within the desert sites
transit.hours: Tours often depart pre-dawn (for geysers) or late afternoon (for sunset sites)
transit.pay: Tours booked and paid through agencies in town
transit.map: Not centrally published; dozens of tour agencies line San Pedro's main street
transit.note: Renting a 4x4 is possible for independent travel, but most visitors join organized tours given the remoteness and altitude

transport.air: El Loa Airport (CJC) in Calama, about 1.5 hr away, with domestic flights from Santiago
transport.bus: Long-distance buses connect to Calama and onward to Santiago (about 20+ hr) or into Bolivia and Argentina
transport.car: Rental cars (ideally 4x4) available in Calama; many sites also require high-altitude driving experience

airport.name: El Loa Airport, Calama
airport.distance: ~100 km (1.5 hr) from San Pedro de Atacama
airport.transport: Shuttle bus or pre-arranged transfer from Calama

net.m: Moderate 4G coverage in town, minimal at remote desert sites
net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes
net.fwn: Free wifi widely available in hotels
net.ap: An Entel or Movistar Chile tourist SIM or eSIM
